question: Should Crabline preserve compatibility for existing directory ownership and `recorderPath` consumers, or intentionally make both behaviors strict breaking contracts in this release?
rationale: The implementation deliberately chooses fail-closed ownership and a new artifact path, and automation cannot determine whether those upgrade breaks match the intended permanent public contract.

options.title: Preserve upgrade compatibility
options.body: Keep the stable `recorderPath`, add a versioned immutable snapshot field, and repair or explicitly migrate mismatched legacy ownership before enforcing strict rejection.

options.title: Approve strict breaking behavior
options.body: Accept the new contracts only with explicit migration documentation and fresh-install plus upgrade proof showing the operator-visible failure and recovery path.

recommendation.title: Preserve upgrade compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep the stable `recorderPath`, add a versioned immutable snapshot field, and repair or explicitly migrate mismatched legacy ownership before enforcing strict rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the repository member implementing the affected contracts and the best available routing candidate for obtaining the required maintainer decision.
